title: Eurycoma longifolia safety and efficacy review
text: Human evidence for Eurycoma longifolia is limited and product standardization, dose, population, and study duration matter when interpreting outcomes.

title: Purified shilajit and testosterone trial
text: A randomized clinical study evaluated purified shilajit at 250 mg twice daily for 90 continuous days in men aged 45 to 55 years. While total and free testosterone showed gradual increases at 90 days, clinical trials do not substantiate an 80% cortisol reduction or doubling of testosterone in 14 days, demonstrating that short-term viral marketing claims significantly exaggerate clinical trial results.

title: Whole Wheat Dietary Fibre and Natural Colour Standards
text: Whole wheat flour and added wheat bran naturally provide dietary fibre fulfilling approximately 28% daily fibre need per serving. In baked brown bread formulations, malt powder and roasted wheat extract are used as natural browning agents without added artificial chemical colours or synthetic dyes.

title: Ashwagandha root extract stress trial
text: A randomized trial evaluated high-concentration ashwagandha root extract for stress and anxiety over 60 days.

title: Creatine fact sheet for consumers
text: Creatine is among supplements discussed by NIH for exercise and athletic performance; effects and safety depend on the product and the person using it.

title: Oral collagen supplementation systematic review
text: A systematic review assessed oral collagen supplements and skin aging outcomes, with study designs and formulations varying across included trials.

title: Green Tea extract and liver injury
text: Green tea extract has been implicated in rare clinically apparent acute liver injury and supplement formulations vary.

title: Whole grain label statements
text: FDA provides guidance on truthful whole-grain label statements and encourages consumers to examine the ingredient list.

title: Food Safety and Standards Labelling Regulations
text: FSSAI food labelling regulations set requirements for ingredient declarations and nutrition information in India.

title: Added sugars on the Nutrition Facts label
text: The U.S. Nutrition Facts label separately declares added sugars to help consumers understand packaged food composition.

title: Guideline: sugars intake for adults and children
text: WHO issued a guideline on reducing free sugars intake across the life course.

title: Pringles Original Potato Crisps ingredients
text: The official United States product page publishes the current ingredient list and nutrition facts for Pringles Original Potato Crisps.

title: Pringles India product listing
text: The official India product listing is a source for checking country-specific product and ingredient disclosures.

title: LAY'S Classic Potato Chips ingredients
text: The official United States product page publishes ingredients and nutrition facts for LAY'S Classic Potato Chips.

title: Trans fat regulations and food labelling
text: FSSAI publishes consumer and regulatory material about fats in packaged food and labelling.

title: Isopropyl Myristate ingredient profile
text: INCIDecoder documents Isopropyl Myristate as an emollient ingredient and lists its comedogenic rating reference.

title: Coconut oil ingredient profile
text: INCIDecoder documents Cocos Nucifera Coconut Oil as an emollient oil and lists its comedogenic rating reference.

title: Fragrance mix allergy
text: DermNet describes fragrance allergy and fragrance mix as a tool used in patch testing for contact allergy.

title: Allergens in cosmetics
text: FDA explains that cosmetic ingredients can cause allergic reactions in some people and consumers should read product labels.

title: Methylisothiazolinone allergy
text: DermNet describes allergic contact dermatitis from methylisothiazolinone and its historical use as a preservative.

title: Sodium lauryl sulfate contact reactions
text: DermNet discusses sodium lauryl sulfate as an irritant consideration in topical and oral-care products.

title: Malassezia folliculitis review
text: A clinical review describes Malassezia folliculitis as a condition that can resemble acne and needs clinical assessment.

title: Acne skin care guidance
text: The American Academy of Dermatology provides general skin-care guidance for people with acne-prone skin.

title: Apple cider vinegar evidence overview
text: NCCIH explains that dietary supplements and food products should not replace evidence-based diabetes care.

title: Dietary supplements overview
text: FDA explains that dietary supplements are regulated differently from conventional foods and drugs.

title: Dietary supplement fact sheets
text: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements publishes consumer and health-professional fact sheets for many nutrients and dietary supplements.

title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids Fact Sheet for Consumers
text: NIH identifies alpha-linolenic acid, eicosapentaenoic acid, and docosahexaenoic acid as the three principal omega-3 fatty acids and distinguishes food and supplement evidence.

title: Vitamin D Fact Sheet for Consumers
text: NIH describes vitamin D as a nutrient involved in calcium absorption and provides age-specific recommended amounts in micrograms and international units.

title: Magnesium Fact Sheet for Consumers
text: NIH notes that magnesium is involved in muscle and nerve function, blood glucose control, blood pressure regulation, and other processes, while high supplemental intakes can have adverse effects.

title: Dietary Supplement Labeling Guide: Claims
text: FDA distinguishes structure or function claims from disease claims and describes substantiation and notification requirements for dietary supplement labels.

title: Summary of Cosmetics Labeling Requirements
text: FDA states that retail cosmetic ingredient declarations generally appear in descending order of predominance, with defined exceptions for some ingredients and color additives.

title: Cosmetic Ingredients
text: FDA explains that companies and individuals marketing cosmetics are legally responsible for the safety of their products and ingredients, while premarket approval rules differ for color additives.

title: Food Allergies and Food Labels
text: FDA explains that labels for packaged foods must identify the food source of major allergens and may do so in an ingredient parenthetical or a contains statement.

title: Gluten and Food Labeling
text: FDA states that voluntary gluten-free, no gluten, free of gluten, and without gluten claims are subject to a definition requiring less than 20 parts per million of gluten.

title: Food Allergen Labeling Guidance
text: FDA guidance explains that foods with two or more ingredients generally declare each ingredient by common or usual name and identifies the source of major food allergens on the label.

title: The Nutrition Facts Label
text: FDA provides consumer guidance for reading serving size, calories, nutrients, and percent Daily Value on the Nutrition Facts label.

title: Fragrance Allergy
text: DermNet describes fragrance allergy as a cause of allergic contact dermatitis and notes that reactions can occur after skin contact with fragrance chemicals.

title: Allergic Contact Dermatitis
text: DermNet describes allergic contact dermatitis as a delayed hypersensitivity reaction and identifies patch testing as a diagnostic approach performed by clinicians.

title: Skin Care Products and Acne
text: The American Academy of Dermatology provides general skin-care guidance for acne-prone skin and advises consumers to consider product labeling when selecting skin-care products.

title: Guideline: Sugars Intake for Adults and Children
text: WHO provides population-level recommendations on reducing free sugars intake and distinguishes them from naturally occurring sugars in intact fruit and milk.

title: Vitamin C Fact Sheet for Consumers
text: NIH describes vitamin C as a water-soluble nutrient and provides consumer information on food sources, supplement forms, recommended amounts, and upper limits.

title: Food Safety and Standards Labelling and Display Regulations, 2020
text: FSSAI's Labelling and Display Regulations prescribe labelling requirements for pre-packaged foods. Except for single-ingredient foods, the ingredient list is declared on the label and ingredients are listed in descending order by weight or volume at manufacture.

title: Food Safety and Standards Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018
text: FSSAI states that food claims must be truthful, unambiguous, meaningful, not misleading, and help consumers comprehend the information provided.

title: Food Products Standards and Food Additives Compendium
text: FSSAI publishes a chapter-wise compendium for food product standards and food additives. The compendium is a ready reference and original notifications prevail where there is an overlap or error.

title: Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024
text: ICMR-NIN's Dietary Guidelines for Indians discuss packaged foods and identify added sugar, added fat, and salt as nutrients of concern when making food choices. The guidance is population-level and does not establish individual product safety.

title: Cosmetics Rules, 2020
text: CDSCO publishes the Cosmetics Rules, 2020. Cosmetics imported or manufactured for India must comply with applicable quality and safety requirements, and a cosmetic may not purport or convey an idea that is false or misleading to an intending user.

title: ASCI guidelines for skin lightening and fairness advertising
text: ASCI's guidance says advertising for skin-lightening or fairness-improvement products should not communicate discrimination based on skin colour or portray darker skin as inferior, unsuccessful, or at a disadvantage in social or professional life.

title: ASCI Code: truthful and honest representation
text: The ASCI Code says advertising descriptions, claims, and comparisons about objectively ascertainable facts should be capable of substantiation and should not mislead consumers through implications, omissions, ambiguity, or exaggeration.
